solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: After silence, hands round the writer's contract

indicators.note: the rest of the wordplay comes after the word for silence, so that word leads

parts.note: SH is the call for silence

indicators.note: the two hands go round the next piece, enclosing it

parts.note: R and L are the right and left hands
the setter speaking of themself: 'the writer has' contracts to I'VE

explanation.surface: A writer's contract is handed over after a hush, as if at a formal signing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contract' looks like a noun in the surface; it is the verb, to shrink.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrivel is to shrink and wrinkle up, so it is a verb synonym of contract.

clue.text: Bad sign, boarding Sierra to travel around, one may end up in jam

definitions.text: one may end up in jam

indicators.note: getting on board, so these pieces go inside the outer pair

parts.note: S is Sierra in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to range is to roam or wander about
bad means evil
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: An omen of ill luck is carried aboard as a ship sets off on a voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam' here is the British sense covering marmalade, a fruit preserve; this bitter orange is the classic marmalade fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bitter Seville orange is the fruit used to make marmalade, so it ends up in a preserve.

clue.text: Cold food after bread is shock

indicators.note: the word for shock is placed after the bread

parts.note: a roll is a small bread loaf
a shock of hair is a mop

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to find a chilly dish served after the bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' is a mass of hair, not a surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet rolled up and eaten cold.

clue.text: Record kept by Crusoe, divided up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from bottom to top
the letters are held within the words that follow, so they are concealed there

explanation.surface: Robinson Crusoe keeps a journal, sectioned into parts, on his island.
explanation.walkthrough: Crusoe famously kept a journal, so 'Record' looks like a diary.
explanation.definitionFit: To video something is to record it on film, so the verb sense matches.

clue.text: Christian left university and rushed to pen article

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, as animals in a fold, so these letters close round the article

parts.note: ran means rushed
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A believer leaves college in a hurry to write a piece for a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' reads as writing the article; it means enclosing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lutheran is a member of the Protestant church founded on Martin Luther's teaching.

clue.text: Many dogs taking the lead off

indicators.note: the lead is the front, so the first letter of the dogs is removed

parts.note: poodles are a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog walker unclips the leads from a large pack of dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like a dog's leash; it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for lots, a large quantity, matching many.

clue.text: Offbeat individual note lifted song, not a tango

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the note's letters are turned upwards

parts.note: do is a note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: one of the letters is dropped, as 'not a' something means without one

parts.note: a ditty is a short simple song
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A quirky person lifts a note in a song but refuses to dance the tango.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns DO into OD; 'not a tango' removes one T from DITTY, leaving DITY.
explanation.definitionFit: An oddity is a strange or eccentric person, an offbeat character.

clue.text: What's in Brontë novel read twice is inspiring English

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the outer letters take in English
novel as an adjective means new, so the letters are made new by rearranging
the word is is taken two times over

explanation.surface: A Brontë novel is read twice over by an English reader who finds it inspiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' reads as a Brontë book but is the anagram signal for READ ISIS, giving DIARESIS; 'inspiring' takes E inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The two dots over the last letter of the surname mark a diaeresis, showing the vowel is sounded separately.

clue.text: Medical department that constantly admits horseman

indicators.note: lets in, so the department's letters go inside

parts.note: ever means always, constantly
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital ward forever taking in a rider who has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a horse rider being admitted as a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: An eventer is a rider, or horse, competing in three-day eventing.

clue.text: Twirling, maybe the ladies one saw approved

indicators.note: spinning round, so the letters for the ladies are turned back to front

parts.note: the ladies is an example of a lav, a lavatory
I is the Roman numeral one
to see someone is to date them, so saw means dated

explanation.surface: A man spins round on the dance floor, approved by the women he went out with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the ladies' is the women's toilet, a LAV, which 'Twirling' turns into VAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Validated means confirmed or officially approved.

clue.text: Great Britain's flipping harsh

parts.note: ace means excellent, great

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters for Britain are reversed

parts.note: BR is an abbreviation for Britain, with the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A grumble that Great Britain is having a really harsh time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British swear word; it reverses BR to RB.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare word for sour or bitter, so harsh in taste or manner.

clue.text: Black grape intertwined with the lush grapevine

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: woven together, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A dark grape tangled among the luxuriant vine leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grapevine' looks like part of the vineyard scene but means informal gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Both terms are idioms for the informal spreading of rumour and news by word of mouth.

clue.text: Vehicle broken by butcher's van in badly neglected state

indicators.note: split open with the next letter inserted

parts.note: a limo is a limousine, a vehicle

indicators.note: the van is the front, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A limousine is crashed into by a butcher's delivery van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'van' looks like a second vehicle; it is the front of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo is being left in a neglected, uncertain state of suspension.

clue.text: Venture into Microsoft's domain is trouble for corporation

parts.note: to enter is to go into
IT, information technology, is Microsoft's field

explanation.surface: A rival company moving into Microsoft's territory spells trouble for the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is an old jokey word for a pot belly, so the trouble is intestinal, not commercial.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteritis is inflammation of the intestine, a stomach complaint for a paunch.

clue.text: Particular sin, snatching diamonds from the east

indicators.note: read from the east, right to left, so the letters run backwards
grabbing and holding, so the gems go inside

parts.note: a lapse is a slip, a moral failing
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A jewel thief's particular sin is grabbing diamonds from Eastern lands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the east' reads the whole LAICEPSE right to left, as an across entry read from its eastern end.
explanation.definitionFit: Especial is a formal synonym of special, meaning particular or notable.

clue.text: Gull, say, overturned angler's device to get fish

parts.note: to gull is to dupe or con

indicators.note: turned upside down, so in a down clue the letters are reversed

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means
a reel winds in an angler's line

explanation.surface: A seagull knocks over a fisherman's tackle to grab a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gull' looks like the bird; it is the verb to deceive.
explanation.definitionFit: The conger is a large marine eel, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Wit's heartless riposte wounded

indicators.note: hurt or damaged, so the letters are twisted
the heart, the central letter, is removed

explanation.surface: A wit's cruel comeback leaves someone hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes the middle O of RIPOSTE; 'wounded' rearranges what is left, RIPSTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Esprit is liveliness of mind and wit, borrowed from French.

clue.text: What some musicians do before and after concert?

definitions.text: What some musicians do before and after concert?

parts.words: What some musicians do before and after concert?
parts.note: string players pick up a bow before playing, and every performer bows to applause afterwards

explanation.surface: A question about the rituals of performers at a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase works twice: violinists literally take up a bow to play, and all accept applause with a bow at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both picking up a violin bow and bending forward to acknowledge applause.

clue.text: Withdraw money that's regularly paid to carry around

indicators.note: the rent holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: rent is paid at regular intervals
CA, short for circa, means around

explanation.surface: A demand to take back rent money that's been paid each month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' suggests taking alternate letters; it just describes rent. 'around' is circa, CA.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to withdraw a statement or belief formally.

clue.text: Intoxicating substance affected air supply

parts.note: camp means exaggerated, affected in manner

indicators.note: read as supplely, bendily, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A drug affecting the air supply, perhaps a dangerous gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is the adverb of supple, not the noun; it rearranges AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Campari is an Italian bitter alcoholic aperitif, so an intoxicating drink.

clue.text: Knight, travelling far, is in China

indicators.note: goes inside the word for friend

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: china plate means mate, a pal

indicators.note: on the move, so the letters are shifted about

explanation.surface: A knight on a long journey ends up in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is rhyming slang, china plate = mate, giving PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsifal is the Arthurian knight of the Grail, hero of Wagner's opera.

clue.text: Car to go wrong on a boring day

indicators.note: drilling into, so these letters go inside the day

parts.note: FRI is short for Friday
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A car breaks down on a dull day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like dull; it means drilling into.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferrari is an Italian make of sports car.

clue.text: Back supporter in my place

parts.note: cor, like my!, is an exclamation of surprise
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: Someone backs a candidate standing in for them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is an exclamation, as in 'my!', giving COR.
explanation.definitionFit: A corset is a stiff undergarment that supports the back and waist.

clue.text: Primary colour nobody's drawing in

indicators.note: pulling inside, so the colour is enclosed

parts.note: none means nobody, with the 's for is
umber is a brown earth colour

explanation.surface: A basic colour that nobody is using in their drawing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primary colour' looks like one phrase; 'Primary' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Number one means first, the chief or principal, like primary.

clue.text: Spray bound to release nitrogen

indicators.note: to let go of, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a bound is a leap, a spring
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: An aerosol spray is certain to give off nitrogen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound to' reads as certain to; 'bound' is a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig or spray is a small shoot or twig of a plant with leaves or flowers.

clue.text: Places quotes from speakers

indicators.note: what speakers say, so the word is as it is heard

parts.note: to quote a source is to cite it

explanation.surface: Positions taking quotations from people giving speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speakers' reads as loudspeakers or orators; it signals the sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Sites are locations, so a plural noun matching places.

clue.text: Do away with Times editorial's introduction

parts.note: eras are long periods of time

indicators.note: the opening, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A demand that The Times scrap the opening of its leading article.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper running this crossword; it means periods.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase something is to wipe it out, getting rid of it entirely.

clue.text: Vessel's sharp, turning and heading for army bases

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, the 's added

indicators.note: turned around, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: tart means sharp in taste

indicators.note: the heading is the top, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A warship turns sharply and heads for army bases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses TART to TRAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Substrata are underlying layers, foundations on which things rest.

clue.text: Cereal, tons on ground mostly

indicators.note: in an across clue, placed after the other piece
most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: grain that is ground has been milled

explanation.surface: Tons of grain have been put through the mill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' reads as the earth; it is milled.
explanation.definitionFit: Millet is a small-seeded grain grass, a cereal crop.

clue.text: Apt to see red snake, in fancy

indicators.note: placed inside the word for fancy

parts.note: to fancy is to wish for
an asp is a venomous snake

explanation.surface: Imagining a snake makes someone see red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see red' looks like being angry at the snake; it defines irritable.
explanation.definitionFit: Waspish means irritable and quick to take offence, so prone to anger.
